text:
Maya (eng-infra): Heads-up — since ~07:10 UTC we've seen streaming token stalls from the usw2-gpupool. App logs show repeated RPC deadlineExceeded on generator calls. Suspecting east-west micro-reordering / jitter on the fabric.

Raj (eng-runtime): Ugh, again. Any pattern by AZ or instance family?

Maya (eng-infra): Mostly us-west-2b -> us-west-2c traffic when requests fan out to GPU workers. QPS spike + tail tokens impacted.

Lin (eng-sre): Can you paste a short tcpdump or packet capture? Also want to know if these servers are using RDMA or kernel TCP for intra-node RPCs.

Maya (eng-infra): Quick tcpdump excerpt: 
```
12:23:45.123456 IP 10.10.5.2.50051 > 10.10.8.7.34012: Flags [P.], seq 345678:345920, ack 987654, win 64240
12:23:45.123459 IP 10.10.5.2.50051 > 10.10.8.7.34012: Flags [P.], seq 345920:346120, ack 987654, win 64240
12:23:45.123462 IP 10.10.5.2.50051 > 10.10.8.7.34012: Flags [P.], seq 345600:345820, ack 987654, win 64240  <-- out of order
```
Shows out-of-order arrival windows, repeated retransmits seen after ~20-30ms.

Raj (eng-runtime): Are we using GRPC over TCP or an RDMA transport for these hot paths? If TCP, TCP reordering can push gRPC into retransmits which kills latency-sensitive streaming.

Maya (eng-infra): These workers use kernel TCP (no RoCE) for now. Some ToRs were recently patched and jumbo frame settings toggled. I'm seeing a mix of MTU 1500 and 9000 across the path.

Nora (eng-platform): That MTU inconsistency rings alarm bells. We had a partial rollout last week where some leaf switches reverted to default MTU during firmware update. Ops ticket #INC-4921 flagged it but was deprioritized.

Lin (eng-sre): Can you run a quick path MTU and reordering check? e.g.
```
# simple check
ping -M do -s 8972 <peer>
# check for reordering (iperf3 with -R?)
iperf3 -c <peer> -P 8 -t 15 --set-mss 8960
```

Maya (eng-infra): Ran iperf3 between two affected hosts: bandwidth looks fine but jitter shows bursts. Sample: 
```
[SUM]   0.00-15.00  sec  9.84 GBytes  5.63 Gbits/sec  0.012 ms avg, 12.3 ms max, 8.9 ms stddev
```
Bursts of ~10-20ms align with the token stalls.

Raj (eng-runtime): Runtime suggestion: increase streaming RPC deadline by small margin for canary (e.g., +50ms) and enable per-request out-of-order tolerance (we can buffer a few packets / reassemble earlier). But that's mitigation, not fix.

Nora (eng-platform): Ops can roll back MTU change or enforce consistent 9000 on whole fabric. Short term, we can route traffic to AZ-local pools to avoid east-west hops. That will cost some capacity but mitigates customer impact.

Maya (eng-infra): I also grabbed ethtool stats on an affected NIC: 
```
rx_errors: 0
rx_missed_errors: 0
rx_nohandler: 0
rx_dropped: 12
tx_dropped: 0
rx_fifo_errors: 0
rx_compressed: 0
```
Not very telling. But on the ToR we see rx_discarded counters spike during incidents.

Lin (eng-sre): Any RDMA counters? If we switch to RoCE, reorder behavior differs.

Maya (eng-infra): Not using RDMA. We do have a couple of hosts in a sub-pool with RoCE enabled for an unrelated internal workload — those didn't show reordering for their traffic since they avoid kernel TCP stacks.

Raj (eng-runtime): That suggests kernel TCP + MTU inconsistency + firmware-induced microbursts = out-of-order arrival. For streaming, gRPC keeps small windows and is sensitive.

Nora (eng-platform): Immediate plan: (1) divert new inference traffic to local-AZ pools (2) bump RPC deadlines by 50ms on canary routes (3) Ops to roll MTU to consistent 1500 or consistent 9000 — prefer to standardize to 9000 but need full rollout window.

Maya (eng-infra): I've applied routing policy for canary traffic to stay AZ-local (started 07:31 UTC). Initial metrics: tail latency improved ~30% for affected requests.

Lin (eng-sre): Good. Please also attach pcap to INC-4921 and tag network-eng. I'll schedule ToR config audit.

Raj (eng-runtime): I'll open a runtime PR to add a graceful reordering buffer for streaming gRPC (config flag) so we have a code knob next time.

deploy-bot: deploy started: runtime/canary: bump-rpc-deadline-50ms -> running in us-west-2b (sha: ae4f2d).

ops-bot: incident INC-4921 created and assigned to network-eng.

Nora (eng-platform): Follow-up: can we quantify cost of AZ-local routing? If we keep it for >24h, we'll need to provision extra reserved capacity or accept higher cross-AZ egress.

Maya (eng-infra): Quick calc: to serve 95th load AZ-local we need +2 small GPU nodes in 2 AZs; estimated extra cost ~ $1.2k/day until full MTU rollout completed.

Raj (eng-runtime): OK let's keep canary for 6 hours, monitor tail tokens, then revert if stable. Also prioritize the code patch; small buffer + deadline knob is low-risk.

Lin (eng-sre): I'll mark this thread as incident context and add the tcpdump + iperf outputs to the incident. Pls drop any other observations here. :thumbsup:
